---
title: "Another crop"
subtitle: "What changes when xdssat runs a crop other than rice, with maize in East Java as the worked example"
---

xdssat runs any crop that DSSAT-CSM simulates from a FileX. The crop comes from the
**template**: every simulated season copies one of its treatments, so the crop, the model,
the planting method and the management all come from that file. The Python code holds no
crop. A new crop needs a template, the crop model's cultivar file, a crop mask, and a few
settings in the experiment file.

[`configs/maize-example.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/maize-example.yml)
is the complete maize example. It is commented for what differs from rice, and
[`configs/rice-java.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/rice-java.yml)
explains every setting in full.

## What changes per crop

| Setting | Rice in Java | Maize in East Java |
|---|---|---|
| `template > file` | `templates/XDRI8601.RIX` (from IRRI's IRMZ8601) | `templates/XDMZ8201.MZX` (from Florida's UFGA8201) |
| `template > crop_model` | `RICER048` (CERES-Rice) | `MZCER048` (CERES-Maize) |
| `cultivars` | codes from `RICER048.CUL` | codes from `MZCER048.CUL` |
| `inputs > crop_mask` | ATR/BPN 2024 rice fields | MapSPAM 2020 maize, physical area |
| `inputs > water_regime` | MoA irrigation classes | MapSPAM 2020 irrigated share of maize |
| `treatments > nitrogen_levels` | 0 to 140 kg N (template levels 0-4) | 0, 60, 116, 120, 180, 401 kg N |
| `treatments > water_regimes` | flooded (level 1), rainfed bunded (level 3) | automatic irrigation (level 4), rainfed (level 0) |
| `treatments > initial_soil_water` | 0.9 | 0.5 |
| `seasons > calendar` | wet 15 Nov, dry 1 Apr (irrigated only) | wet 15 Nov, dry 15 Mar (both regimes) |
| scenario `cultivar_coefficients` | e.g. `TCLDF` | `P1`, `P2`, `P5`, `G2`, `G3`, `PHINT` |

Write out every section of a new experiment file. A section left out takes the default
of `configs/rice-java.yml`, which is the rice case study.

## The template

Any DSSAT experiment file of the crop can be the template. It must have:

- **One treatment for every water regime and N rate** the experiment file asks for. A run
  finds the treatment by its irrigation level (MI) and fertilizer level (MF);
  `treatments > water_regimes > template_level` and `treatments > nitrogen_levels` point at
  them. Level 0 means none: no irrigation section, or no fertilizer.
- **A planting date** in its planting level: every other date of the treatment moves with
  it, so management keeps its timing relative to planting.
- **A sowing depth** (`PLDP`) between 0 and 100 cm. The engine stops without it for every
  crop except sugarcane (`ipexp.for:1024-1026`).
- **`PLME` S (seed)** for crops other than rice, or a transplant weight (`SDWTPL`) with `PLME`
  T: a non-rice crop with `PLME` T and no `SDWTPL` stops the run (`ipexp.for:1047-1051`).
- No soil analysis (SA), chemical (MC) or tillage (MT) levels in the treatments it uses.

The engine reads the crop code from the experiment code in the first line of the template
(`UFGA8201MZ`: `MZ`), and the run writes its experiment files with the template's own
extension (`.MZX`). Cultivars other than the template's go into the template's cultivar
level, so a variety needs only its line in the cultivar file. CERES-Maize also needs the
ecotype file (`MZCER048.ECO`) and stops when a cultivar's ecotype is missing from it
(`MZ_PHENOL.for:283-303`); xdssat copies the engine's ecotype and species files into every run.

### The maize template

`python scripts/make_templates.py` writes `templates/XDMZ8201.MZX` from DSSAT's
`UFGA8201.MZX` [@bennett1986]: maize hybrid McCurdy 84aa sown on 26 Feb 1982 at
Gainesville, Florida, 7.2 plants/m2 in 61 cm rows, 7 cm deep. This is the CERES-Maize
example of the DSSAT ecosystem chapter [@hoogenboom2019, section 12.1].

| Treatments | Water | N |
|---|---|---|
| 1-6 | the experiment's own: rainfed (one 13 mm irrigation 6 days after sowing), irrigated, vegetative stress | 116 or 401 kg N/ha in the experiment's own splits |
| 7-12 | automatic irrigation (MI 4, SM 2) | 0, 60, 116, 120, 180, 401 kg N/ha |
| 13-18 | rainfed, no irrigation (MI 0, SM 1) | 0, 60, 116, 120, 180, 401 kg N/ha |

The 60, 120 and 180 kg N levels are urea, incorporated at 5 cm, one third at sowing and two
thirds 35 days after sowing. This split is an xdssat assumption, not part of the experiment.
The experiment's own levels give their first dose 40 days (116 kg N) and 17 days (401 kg N)
after sowing.

## Water regimes of an upland crop

A rice template floods the irrigated field and holds rain behind bunds in the rainfed one.
An upland crop needs neither: the maize template uses the engine's automatic irrigation for
the irrigated regime and no irrigation for the rainfed one.

- **Automatic irrigation.** The treatment's simulation controls set `IRRIG` to `A`. When the
  plant-available water of the top `IMDEP` cm (30) falls to `ITHRL` percent (50), the engine
  adds enough water to bring it back to `ITHRU` percent (100), plus 5 mm
  (`IRRIG.for:820-840, 1025-1062`). It irrigates from the simulation start to maturity
  (`IRRIG.for:810-813`). The efficiency comes from `IREFF` of the automatic row; `EFIR` of
  the irrigation section and the method `IMETH` are not used for automatic irrigation
  (`IRRIG.for:761-766`). It needs no irrigation level, so the maize template's level 4 only
  marks the treatment.
- **Rainfed.** Irrigation level 0 with `IRRIG` R applies no water (`IRRIG.for:702-714`).

Flood, bund and puddling operations (`IR006` to `IR011`) are written for paddy rice. The
engine does not limit them to rice, so they would also flood a maize field.

## Settings that act on maize

| Setting | CERES-Maize | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `slpf`, `slpf_rainfed`, `slpf_table` | multiplies daily carbohydrate, as in rice | `MZ_GROSUB.for:1192-1193` |
| SLNF (soil file) | scales organic matter mineralisation with the CERES method (`MESOM` G); ignored with CENTURY (`MESOM` P) | `SoilOrg.for:673`, `SOMDEC_C.for:24` |
| `cultivar_coefficients: TCLDF` | rice only: refused for a maize run | `RICER048.CUL` |
| cold | the crop dies after `CDAY` (15) days with Tmin at or below `TSEN` (6 C), from `MZCER048.ECO` | `MZ_GROSUB.for:1686-1710` |
| `environment: co2` | acts through a radiation-use multiplier table of `MZCER048.SPE` (1.02 at 400 ppm, 1.05 at 570 ppm) | `MZ_GROSUB.for:1133-1141` |
| `initial_soil_water` | crop-independent | `IPSLIN.for:100-124` |
| harvest | at maturity (`HARVS` M); the summary has the same columns as rice | `AUTHAR.for:151-153` |

Source references are to the DSSAT-CSM 4.8 code [@dssatcsmos].

## Crop mask and water regime for maize

The crop mask can be any map of the crop (see [Input data](data.qmd#crop-mask)). The
example uses MapSPAM 2020 [@spam2020], CC BY 4.0, from the physical-area zip
(`spam2020V2r2_global_physical_area.geotiff.zip`):

- `spam2020_V2r2_global_A_MAIZ_A.tif`: maize physical area, all technologies, ha per pixel
  (5 arc-minutes, about 9 km). xdssat reads each pixel as 10 x 10 sub-points of about 900 m.
- `spam2020_V2r2_global_A_MAIZ_I.tif`: irrigated maize. Divided by `_A`, it gives the
  irrigated share of each pixel (`values: ratio`).

A general cropland class (ESA WorldCover class 40) does not say which crop grows where; with
it, maize is assumed on all cropland.

## Run the example

Unzip the two maize files into `<paths > inputs>/spam2020/`, fill in the paths of a copy of
the experiment file (or set the `XDSSAT_*` environment variables), then:

```bash
python scripts/make_templates.py
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/maize-example.yml
python scripts/prepare_layers.py --config configs/maize-example.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py --config configs/maize-example.yml --aoi ejava
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/maize-example.yml --check
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/maize-example.yml
```

**Tested** on East Java, agricultural years 2016-2020, uniform calendar, McCurdy 84aa, 120 kg
N, SLPF 1 (uncalibrated): 582 strata in 492 weather cells, 282,804 ha of maize (38,704 ha
irrigated), 5,820 seasons, none failed, 66 s on 32 workers. Area-weighted grain yield (HWAH,
dry matter):

| | wet season | dry season |
|---|---|---|
| automatic irrigation | 9,962 kg/ha | 10,536 kg/ha |
| rainfed | 10,079 kg/ha | 9,061 kg/ha |

Median irrigation was 27 mm in the wet season and 109 mm in the dry season; rainfed seasons
got none. FAOSTAT gives Indonesia's maize yield as 5.31, 5.30, 5.31, 6.14 and 5.53 t/ha for
2016 to 2020 [@faostat_qcl], a mean of 5.52 t/ha. The uncalibrated simulation (9,663 kg/ha
over all seasons) is about 1.75 times that. Calibration (SLPF, cultivar) closes the gap.

**Tested** on a 40-cell sample, 2017-2018, the same settings except the N rate. Area-weighted
yield in kg/ha:

| kg N/ha | irrigated wet | irrigated dry | rainfed wet | rainfed dry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2,696 | 2,968 | 2,909 | 2,662 |
| 60 | 6,619 | 6,919 | 6,744 | 5,548 |
| 116 (the experiment's late split) | 8,254 | 8,721 | 8,608 | 6,214 |
| 120 | 9,718 | 10,216 | 10,032 | 7,491 |
| 180 | 10,354 | 11,022 | 10,850 | 7,426 |
| 401 | 10,370 | 11,019 | 10,905 | 6,317 |

Yield rises with N to about 180 kg N. Rainfed dry-season maize levels off near 7.4 t/ha,
where water limits it.

Seasons are longer in cool cells. In 36 of the 492 cells (mean daily Tmin 16.7 C, against
23.1 C in the others: Tengger, Ijen, Argopuro, Arjuno, Lawu, Wilis), rainfed maize took more
than 150 days from sowing to maturity in some years: 284 of the 5,820 seasons, 4.6% of the
area. Thermal time accumulates slowly there. Two more rainfed seasons (dry season of 2020)
were not mature when the 220 days of weather of `run > season_days` ended, and have no
maturity date in `summary.csv`.

## Outputs of another crop

The run folder has the same files for every crop (see
[Getting started](getting-started.md#outputs)). The crop is recorded in `run_info.json`
(`crop`: code, name, model, model name, from the engine's `DETAIL.CDE` and
`SIMULATION.CDE`), and the netCDF names it in its `title`, `crop` and `crop_model`
attributes. The area variables are `crop_area` (per system) and `crop_area_total`. Rice
runs also carry them as `rice_area` and `rice_area_total`, the names of files written
before other crops. A run folder without `crop` in `run_info.json` is rice.

The onset setting `seasons > onset > planting_after_days` is the days from rainfall onset
to planting (sowing or transplanting). Older files call it `transplant_after_days`; that
name is still read.
